svg.title: Research map
svg.desc: Isometric map of data systems for AI agents. Parts: People and agents; Agent; Meaning (current work); Data; Definition check (current work); Change over time; Infrastructure. An animation follows one BIRD question: two code definitions were swapped, the agent answered 22 instead of 13 with no warning, and a definition check would have caught the swap before the agent read the codes.
svg.text: I study data systems for AI agents: where their answers go wrong,
and which checks inside the system catch it.

g.text: A person asks: “How many accounts that choose issuance after transaction
It reads the definitions of the statement codes. Two of them were swapped.
Its query runs without an error and counts the accounts that have the
It answers 22. The right answer is 13. It gives no warning.
The person acts on 22. In my pilot this happened in all 9 runs, across 3
A definition check would have caught the swap before the agent read the
codes. That check is my current work.
The check runs where the data lives, not at answer time: on each new batch
of rows, and on each database branch before a merge.
When the data or a definition changes, it re-runs only the checks that the
change touches. That keeps it cheap at scale.
